setup.title: Setup
setup.intro: Create the dashboard account. The server shows the setup code on its screen and on SSH login.
setup.hint: The account is for the dashboard only, not for SSH. The server name is optional; the server is then reachable as <name>.local.
login.title: Log in
storage.title: Disks
storage.hint: Disks with ext4, XFS or Btrfs are added with their data. Blank disks can be formatted; for other disks Dahlia first copies the data to /mnt/user, then formatting is possible.
storage.confirm_remove: Unmount {path} and remove it from Dahlia? The data stays on the disk.
jobs.title: Jobs
updates.title: Updates
updates.hint: snapper takes a snapshot before and after every update; it can be booted from the boot menu.
updates.checking: Checking for updates, this can take a minute …
updates.none: The system is up to date.
updates.state_failed: Update failed. See the log of dahlia-update.service.
account.changed: Password changed. Other sessions were logged out.
error.too_many_attempts: Too many failed attempts. Please wait five minutes.
error.username: Username: 2 to 32 characters, lower case letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter.
error.password: The password must be at least 10 characters long.
agent.unavailable: The system service dahlia-agent is not running.
agent.forbidden: The dashboard may not use the system service.
agent.timeout: The system service does not answer.
apps.title: Apps
apps.hint: Apps run as Docker containers. Depending on the choice at install, their data lives on the array (/mnt/user/appdata) or on the system SSD (/srv/appdata).
apps.catalog_empty: The catalog is empty. “Refresh catalog” loads it.
apps.confirm_delete_data: Also delete the data in {path}? “Cancel” keeps it.
domains.title: Domains and certificates
domains.hint: Apps are reachable at https://<app>.<domain>, with mDNS also at https://<app>.local. The local Dahlia CA issues the certificate.
domains.domain_hint: Use a domain under home.arpa, e.g. dahlia.home.arpa. Multi-level .local names do not work. A domain outside home.arpa makes Dahlia create a new CA that devices have to import again.
domains.dns_hint: Create these records in your local DNS (AdGuard Home: Filters > DNS rewrites; Pi-hole or router: local DNS record).
domains.ca_hint: Import the CA as trusted once on every device; the browser then stops warning. Compare the fingerprint with the one shown after login (console or SSH) first. The CA can only sign names under .local, home.arpa, your own domain and private IP addresses.
domains.saved: Saved. Certificate and proxy are updated.
domains.saved_new_ca: Saved. There is a new CA: import it again on all devices.
apps.refreshed: Catalog as of {when}. Dahlia reloads it every 6 hours and then shows available updates.
apps.confirm_lan: The app also opens these ports on the network: {ports}
storage.pool_user: What apps and shares see: cache and all data disks together.
storage.pool_storage: All data disks together, without the cache.
storage.pool_cache: SSD for new files; the mover moves them to the array at night.
account.hostname_hint: The server is then reachable as <name>.local. Certificate and app addresses are updated.
docker.hint: All containers on the server, including those not installed from the app catalog. CPU and RAM refresh every 5 seconds.
docker.name: Name
docker.confirm_prune: Delete all images no container uses and empty the build cache? Images of stopped apps are kept.
app.title: {host} · Dahlia, I love you ♥
settings.ntp: Set the time automatically from the internet (NTP)
settings.net_hint: After a change you have 3 minutes to confirm it. Without confirmation Dahlia restores the old settings.
settings.net_confirm:
Change the network settings?
If the address changes, open the dashboard at the new address or via https://<server name>.local and confirm there within 3 minutes. Otherwise Dahlia restores the old settings.
settings.net_started: Changing the network. Please confirm within {s} seconds.
settings.net_pending: New network settings are active. They are reverted in {s} seconds.
settings.net_reverted: The last network change was not confirmed and has been reverted.
settings.spindown_hint: Hard disks go to standby after this time without access. SSDs and NVMe are not affected. Some USB enclosures do not support it.
settings.spindown_failed:
Saved, but not applied to every disk:
{disks}
settings.firewall_hint: Access only from local networks and only on ports a service or app uses. Container ports cannot be reached from the internet.
settings.firewall_off: Firewall off: every port is open to anyone who can reach the server.
settings.firewall_disable_confirm: Really turn off the firewall? All services are then reachable without filtering.
settings.schedules_hint: When the mover, SnapRAID sync and scrub run automatically. Sync should run after the mover.
shares.title: SMB shares
shares.hint: Each share is a folder under /mnt/user, so it spans the cache and the data disks. Windows: \\{host}.local\<share>, macOS: smb://{host}.local/<share>.
shares.no_pool: /mnt/user is not mounted. Add a data disk under Disks first, then shares can be created.
shares.name: Name
shares.confirm_remove:
Remove share {name}?
The folder and its files stay on the array.
shares.time_machine: Offer as a Time Machine target for Macs
shares.users_hint: Accounts for shares only, without login on the server. Separate from the dashboard account.
shares.no_users: No SMB users yet. Create one below.
shares.confirm_user_remove:
Delete SMB user {name}?
They lose access to all shares. Their files stay.
security.public_hint: Everyone on the network can read and write without a password.
security.secure_hint: Everyone on the network can read without a password. Only users with "read and write" may write.
security.private_hint: Only the selected users have access.
notify.title: Notifications
notify.hint: Dahlia reports SMART warnings, hot disks, full disks, failed jobs and UPS events. Checks run every 10 minutes.
ups.title: UPS
ups.name: UPS name
ups.hint: NUT detects a USB UPS on its own. For a UPS on a Synology or another NUT server, enter its address, UPS name and credentials.
storage.format_warning: {path} ({model}, {size}) gets a GPT partition table and a new filesystem. Afterwards you can add the disk in a role.
storage.fs_xfs: XFS (recommended for data and parity disks)
storage.formatted: {path} is formatted. Now pick a role and add the disk.
storage.import_text: {path} ({fs}, {size}) is mounted read-only. Dahlia copies everything into a new share under /mnt/user and then compares every file. Only then can the disk be formatted. Owners and Windows permissions are not copied.
storage.format_warning_imported: The data of {path} ({model}, {size}) has been imported. The disk now gets a new GPT partition table and a new filesystem; everything on it is erased.
import.done: {path} has been copied to {target} and verified.
import.finished: Data imported. The disk can be formatted now.
install.title: Set up {name}
install.folders_hint: The app sees these folders. "Change" picks another folder on the system SSD or the array; the path inside the app stays the same.
install.pool_missing: No array set up: the app goes to the system SSD. You can add data disks later.
install.download: Images are downloaded; this can take a few minutes
install.appdata: The app's settings and database are kept in {path}.
folder.title: Choose folder
folder.missing: This folder does not exist yet; it is created on install.
diag.title: Diagnostics bundle
diag.hint: An archive with versions, services, journal, disks, network, Docker and app state for a bug report. Passwords, tokens, keys and app secrets stay out; file, share and user names can appear. Look through it before posting it publicly.
diag.working: Creating it, this takes up to a minute …
auto.title: Automatic security updates
auto.hint: Daily around 06:00, only from the Debian security archive. All other updates (Dahlia, Docker, Debian point releases) are installed above, with a snapshot before.
auto.reboot_hint: Some updates (kernel, libc) only take effect after a restart. Without the automatic restart Dahlia reports when one is needed.
auto.reboot_needed: A restart is needed for installed updates to take effect.
auto.reboot_needed_pkgs: A restart is needed for installed updates to take effect ({list}).
parity.title: Parity
parity.checked_value: {pct} % of the array at least once
parity.schedule_hint: Sync daily at 04:30, check (scrub) Sundays at 06:00; change the times under Settings → Schedules.
parity.what: The parity (SnapRAID) can restore one failed data disk per parity disk, as of the last sync. The cache and appdata are not protected; the backup covers those.
parity.restore_step1: Remove the failed data disk under Disks.
parity.restore_step2: Install the new disk, format it and add it as a data disk. It gets the same number.
parity.restore_step3: Pick the disk here and restore it. The files come back from the parity and are verified afterwards.
parity.restore_confirm: Restore the files of {disk} from the parity? Depending on the size this takes hours. No sync runs until it is done.
parity.threshold: Stop the sync from this many deleted files
parity.threshold_hint: Protects against an unmounted or accidentally emptied disk: the sync waits until you confirm.
parity.running_mover: The mover is running; sync and check wait until it is done.
parity.no_parity: No parity set up yet. Add a disk as parity under Disks; it must be at least as large as the largest data disk. Then sync here.
parity.no_data: There are no data disks yet. Add them under Disks.
parity.problems: The parity cannot run like this: {list}
parity.unmounted: Not mounted: {list}. Sync and check only run when all disks are there.
parity.bad: The last check found {n} bad blocks. They can be repaired from the parity.
parity.repair_confirm: Repair {n} bad blocks from the parity and check them again?
parity.blocked: The last sync was stopped: {n} files deleted, more than the limit of {threshold}. Check that all disks are mounted and the deletions were intended.
parity.force_confirm: The {n} deleted files will then be gone from the parity as well and cannot be restored. Sync anyway?
parity.interrupted: A sync was interrupted. Run it again so the parity is complete.
backup.disk_hint: The backup goes to the folder dahlia-backup on this disk. Safest is a disk outside the array, e.g. a USB disk.
backup.sftp_hint: After saving, Dahlia shows an SSH key. Add it to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of this user on the server.
backup.stop_apps: Stop apps briefly during the backup (recommended, databases may be inconsistent otherwise)
backup.what: Backed up: the data of all apps (appdata), their settings, /etc/dahlia and the dashboard accounts, encrypted with restic. Shares such as films and photos are not included. Kept: 7 daily, 4 weekly and 6 monthly snapshots.
backup.schedule_hint: Runs daily at 02:00; change the time under Settings → Schedules.
backup.restore_hint: Restoring replaces an app's data with the chosen snapshot; the app is stopped briefly.
backup.restore_confirm: Reset {what} to the state of {time}? Newer data of this app is lost.
backup.saved: Backup target saved. The daily backup is on.
terminal.hint: Log in with this user's Linux password, as over SSH. Root with sudo. Disconnects after 15 minutes without input; every session is in the system log.
terminal.ready: Choose a user and click Connect.
terminal.unavailable: The terminal service (dahlia-terminal) is not running.
apps.gpu_used: Uses the GPU (/dev/dri) for video and AI.
apps.gpu_none: Can use a GPU; none found, runs on the CPU.
snap.title: System snapshots
snap.hint: snapper records the state of the system before and after every update. A rollback restarts the server with that state. Packages and /etc go back; /home, /root, the logs, Dahlia's settings, apps and Docker data stay as they are, as do /srv and the array.
snap.rollback_confirm: Reset the system to snapshot {n} ({date}) and restart right away? The current state is kept as a separate subvolume.
snap.rollback_post_hint: This is the state after an update. To undo the update, pick snapshot {pre} (before).
snap.rollback_started: Rollback running, the server restarts in a moment.
snap.running: Rollback running, the server restarts in a moment.
snap.rolled_back: The system was reset to snapshot {n} on {time}.
snap.old_hint: Before every rollback the state at that time is kept here. Once the system runs as it should, delete it to free the space.
